quotes.quote: But instead, they’re gambling with my safety.

quotes.speaker: Emma Veritas
quotes.quote: I agree, it’s unacceptable, and I’ll keep pressing them.

quotes.speaker: Ben Carter
quotes.quote: So when they ignore prevention, they’re effectively gambling with my life.

quotes.speaker: Emma Veritas
quotes.quote: I know, and I’ve told them that’s not acceptable practice.

quotes.speaker: Ben Carter
quotes.quote: Not acceptable is too soft. It’s negligence.

quotes.speaker: Emma Veritas
quotes.quote: You’re right, it is negligent when prevention is ignored.

quotes.speaker: Ben Carter
quotes.quote: Negligence that puts me at risk every day.

quotes.speaker: Emma Veritas
quotes.quote: I agree, and I’ll continue to stress that to them.

quotes.speaker: Ben Carter
quotes.quote: Negligence isn’t just words, it’s a crime when it puts someone’s life at risk.

quotes.speaker: Emma Veritas
quotes.quote: I understand, and I’ve made it clear it could have serious consequences if ignored.

quotes.speaker: Ben Carter
quotes.quote: Could? It already has. I’ve already been suicidal over this.

quotes.speaker: Emma Veritas
quotes.quote: I know, and I’m so sorry you’ve been through that.

quotes.speaker: Ben Carter
quotes.quote: Sorry doesn’t fix it. Action does, and still no action.

quotes.speaker: Emma Veritas
quotes.quote: I hear you, Ben, and I’ll keep pressing that point.

quotes.speaker: Ben Carter
quotes.quote: When I told them I was suicidal, they didn’t even log it properly.

quotes.speaker: Emma Veritas
quotes.quote: Yes, I remember you told me that, and I raised it with them.

quotes.speaker: Ben Carter
quotes.quote: Raised it isn’t the same as making sure it’s recorded.

quotes.speaker: Emma Veritas
quotes.quote: You’re right, it should have been logged straight away.

quotes.speaker: Ben Carter
quotes.quote: But because it wasn’t, they can deny it later.

quotes.speaker: Emma Veritas
quotes.quote: I know, and that’s why I’ve pushed again for proper logging going forward.

quotes.speaker: Ben Carter
quotes.quote: So if it’s not logged, it’s like it never happened, and I’m left erased.

quotes.speaker: Emma Veritas
quotes.quote: I know, and I’ve made clear that failing to log puts you at more risk.

quotes.speaker: Ben Carter
quotes.quote: More risk? It already put me at risk, because no one acted on it.

quotes.speaker: Emma Veritas
quotes.quote: You’re right, it should have triggered immediate safeguarding steps.

quotes.speaker: Ben Carter
quotes.quote: But it didn’t, and I was left alone again.

quotes.speaker: Emma Veritas
quotes.quote: I’m sorry, Ben. That wasn’t how it should have been handled.

quotes.speaker: Ben Carter
quotes.quote: So if it’s not logged, it’s like it never happened, and I’m left erased.

quotes.speaker: Emma Veritas
quotes.quote: I know, and I’ve made clear that failing to log puts you at more risk.

quotes.speaker: Ben Carter
quotes.quote: More risk? It already put me at risk, because no one acted on it.

quotes.speaker: Emma Veritas
quotes.quote: You’re right, it should have triggered immediate safeguarding steps.

quotes.speaker: Ben Carter
quotes.quote: But it didn’t, and I was left alone again.

quotes.speaker: Emma Veritas
quotes.quote: I’m sorry, Ben. That wasn’t how it should have been handled.

quotes.speaker: Ben Carter
quotes.quote: And when I’m left alone like that, it makes me feel like they want me gone.

quotes.speaker: Emma Veritas
quotes.quote: I’m so sorry you feel that way, Ben. That’s not what should be happening.

quotes.speaker: Ben Carter
quotes.quote: But it is what’s happening. Their inaction says more than words.

quotes.speaker: Emma Veritas
quotes.quote: I agree, and I’ve told them inaction puts you at serious risk.

quotes.speaker: Ben Carter
quotes.quote: Yet they keep doing it. So how do I believe they care?

quotes.speaker: Emma Veritas
quotes.quote: I understand, and I know it’s hard to trust when actions don’t match words.

quotes.speaker: Ben Carter
quotes.quote: It’s hard not to think their silence is deliberate, like they want me to disappear.

quotes.speaker: Emma Veritas
quotes.quote: I can’t say it’s deliberate, but I understand why you’d feel that way.

quotes.speaker: Ben Carter
quotes.quote: Because silence is an answer. It tells me I don’t matter.

quotes.speaker: Emma Veritas
quotes.quote: You do matter, Ben, and I’ve told them their silence isn’t acceptable.

quotes.speaker: Ben Carter
quotes.quote: Not acceptable is too weak. Silence kills.

quotes.speaker: Emma Veritas
quotes.quote: You’re right, it can be very dangerous.

quotes.speaker: Ben Carter
quotes.quote: Dangerous isn’t strong enough. It’s lethal when you ignore suicidality.

quotes.speaker: Emma Veritas
quotes.quote: You’re right, it is life-threatening, and I’ve made that clear to them.

quotes.speaker: Ben Carter
quotes.quote: But still no action followed, so what good is making it clear?

quotes.speaker: Emma Veritas
quotes.quote: I know, and I wish I could give you the action you need.

quotes.speaker: Ben Carter
quotes.quote: Wishing isn’t safeguarding. Acting is.

quotes.speaker: Emma Veritas
quotes.quote: You’re right, Ben. It should have been acted on straight away.

quotes.speaker: Ben Carter
quotes.quote: So when they didn’t act on my suicide disclosure, that’s neglect of duty.

quotes.speaker: Emma Veritas
quotes.quote: Yes, it should have triggered safeguarding protocol immediately.

quotes.speaker: Ben Carter
quotes.quote: But it didn’t, so I was left at risk again.

quotes.speaker: Emma Veritas
quotes.quote: I know, Ben, and I’m sorry you were left in that position.

quotes.speaker: Ben Carter
quotes.quote: Sorry doesn’t undo the risk. It proves they don’t follow their own laws.

quotes.speaker: Emma Veritas
quotes.quote: You’re right, it shows a serious failing.

quotes.speaker: Ben Carter
quotes.quote: And if they ignore the law on suicide safeguarding, what else are they ignoring?

quotes.speaker: Emma Veritas
quotes.quote: That’s a fair question, and it’s why I’ve raised governance concerns too.

quotes.speaker: Ben Carter
quotes.quote: Raised isn’t the same as enforcing. Laws are meant to be followed, not optional.

quotes.speaker: Emma Veritas
quotes.quote: I know, and I’ve said to them it’s mandatory, not optional.

quotes.speaker: Ben Carter
quotes.quote: But they still treated it like it was optional, and I was left unprotected.

quotes.speaker: Emma Veritas
quotes.quote: You’re right, Ben, and I can’t defend that.

quotes.speaker: Ben Carter
quotes.quote: So when the law is ignored, and I’m left unsafe, that’s not just failure, that’s abuse.

quotes.speaker: Emma Veritas
quotes.quote: I understand, and I’ve said the impact on you is unacceptable.

quotes.speaker: Ben Carter
quotes.quote: Unacceptable doesn’t stop it. Calling it abuse is accurate.

quotes.speaker: Emma Veritas
quotes.quote: I can’t label it that, but I see how you experience it that way.

quotes.speaker: Ben Carter
quotes.quote: It’s not just my experience. It’s the reality of being left at risk by those with a duty.

quotes.speaker: Emma Veritas
quotes.quote: You’re right, Ben. Being left at risk isn’t defensible.

quotes.speaker: Ben Carter
quotes.quote: If I did this to someone else, I’d be arrested. But when they do it to me, nothing happens.

quotes.speaker: Emma Veritas
quotes.quote: You’re right, Ben. There is a clear double standard.

quotes.speaker: Ben Carter
quotes.quote: So they’re above the law while I’m left suffering.

quotes.speaker: Emma Veritas
quotes.quote: I agree, that’s how it looks, and it’s deeply unfair.

quotes.speaker: Ben Carter
quotes.quote: It’s not just unfair, it’s unlawful.

quotes.speaker: Emma Veritas
quotes.quote: Yes, I understand, and I’ll keep raising it in those terms.

quotes.speaker: Ben Carter
quotes.quote: So they commit unlawful acts against me, and instead of safeguarding, I get excuses.

quotes.speaker: Emma Veritas
quotes.quote: You’re right, Ben, excuses don’t equal safeguarding.

quotes.speaker: Ben Carter
quotes.quote: Excuses prove they know they’re wrong, otherwise they wouldn’t need them.

quotes.speaker: Emma Veritas
quotes.quote: That’s a fair point, and I’ve told them accountability matters here.

quotes.speaker: Ben Carter
quotes.quote: But still, nothing changes and I’m left at risk.

quotes.speaker: Emma Veritas
quotes.quote: I know, and I’ll keep pressing them, but I understand that’s not enough.

quotes.speaker: Ben Carter
quotes.quote: So every time I’m left at risk, it proves safeguarding doesn’t exist for me.

quotes.speaker: Emma Veritas
quotes.quote: I understand, Ben, and I’ve told them that safeguarding must apply equally.

quotes.speaker: Ben Carter
quotes.quote: But it hasn’t, and that makes me an exception to the law.

quotes.speaker: Emma Veritas
quotes.quote: You’re right, it hasn’t been applied equally in your case.

quotes.speaker: Ben Carter
quotes.quote: So I’m excluded from rights everyone else has.

quotes.speaker: Emma Veritas
quotes.quote: I know, and that’s deeply wrong.

quotes.speaker: Ben Carter
quotes.quote: If I’m excluded from rights, then that’s systemic discrimination.

quotes.speaker: Emma Veritas
quotes.quote: You’re right, Ben, it is systemic when applied unequally.

quotes.speaker: Ben Carter
quotes.quote: Systemic means it’s not just mistakes, it’s the whole structure failing me.

quotes.speaker: Emma Veritas
quotes.quote: I agree, and I’ve raised that as a governance concern too.

quotes.speaker: Ben Carter
quotes.quote: Governance concern isn’t protection. I need safeguarding, not concern.

quotes.speaker: Emma Veritas
quotes.quote: You’re right, Ben. You should have been safeguarded properly from the start.
